title: Responder workflow patterns and customer chronicle
author: Priya Anand
content:
Overview

This document describes a lightweight, practical responder workflow for common Redwood Inference incidents, a structured on-call rotation pattern, a reusable postmortem scaffold, a concise game-day syllabus, and customer-facing comms templates captured as a single "chronicle". The goal is to reduce diagnostic time, standardize communication, and make post-incident learning frictionless.

Scope

- Services in scope: inference-gateway, router, kv-cache, dedicated-proxy, console-api, model-allocator
- Incident classes: latency SLO regressions, capacity exhaustion, KV-cache corruption, model-quality regressions (e2e), control-plane authentication failures

Roles and responsibilities

- First Responder (FR): the primary on-call engineer who acknowledges alerts, performs initial triage, applies containment, and coordinates the bridge.
- Platform Pager (PP): escalates for infrastructure-level failures (GPU OOM, scheduler unavailable).
- On-call Lead (OCL): coordinates cross-team escalation and customer comms if incident is Sev 1/2.
- SRE Manager: approves major mitigations (capacity increases, region failovers) and postmortem sign-off.
- Customer Success Liaison (CSL): drafts customer notices for impacted tenants and liaises with legal/compliance for regulated customers.

Incident severity ladder (summary)

1. Sev 1 — Critical outage: multi-region unavailability, >99.9% requests failing, SLA breach imminent.
2. Sev 2 — Major degradation: P99 latency above SLO for >10 minutes or a sustained error rate increase affecting >5% of requests.
3. Sev 3 — Partial impact/isolated: single-customer or single-region degradation, transient errors.

SLOs and alert thresholds (operational table)

| SLO | Measurement | Alert threshold | Pager level |
|-----|-------------|-----------------|-------------|
| Availability | 99.95% 30d | 99.7% in 30m window | Sev 1 |
| API p99 (small models) | <250ms | p99 >350ms for 10m | Sev 2 |
| Error rate | <0.5% overall | >2% sustained for 5m | Sev 2 |
| KV cache hit | >85% | drop >20pp over 10m | Sev 2 |

First responder runbook (quick checklist)

1. Acknowledge page within 2 minutes. If no ack, escalation to PP after 5 minutes.
2. Triage: gather key facts and fill incident stub in Slack channel #inc-bridge:
   - service: inference-gateway
   - region(s): us-west-2
   - symptoms: increased 500s from backend, p99 from 220ms -> 1200ms
   - start time (observed): 2025-02-14T09:12:00Z
3. Containment: switch traffic to fallback model-variant or reduce batch-size using /ops/traffic/route endpoint. Example: curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/route -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","variant":"fallback-v1"}' 
4. Verify: confirm traffic routing change in telemetry within 60s. If not successful, proceed to failover steps.
5. Communicate: post an initial status message (template below) and tag OCL if Sev >=2.
6. Prepare evidence: collect top 10 traces, scheduler logs, recent deploys (git commit IDs), and alert timeline.

Containment & mitigation patterns (decision ladder)

- Latency spike (p99 regression): reduce batch-size, enable CPU-side inference fallback, or route to lower-capacity but lower-latency region.
- Capacity exhaust (GPU OOM or queue saturation): throttle non-tenant-critical routes, increase replica count on dedicated-proxy, or trigger burst capacity policy for Dedicated pools.
- KV-cache corruption: roll back to previous healthy snapshot, disable cache writes, and run asynchronous reconciliation job.
- Model-quality regression: pin to previous model version and re-run eval suite on canary traffic.

Escalation matrix (names are examples for practice)

- 0–5m: First Responder -> acknowledgement or escalate to Platform Pager
- 5–20m: Platform Pager investigates; if infra-impacting escalate to On-call Lead
- 20–60m: On-call Lead coordinates cross-team mitigation and engages CSL for customer notices
- >60m: SRE Manager and Head of Product brief execs and decide on extended mitigations or customer credits

Status page and customer comms templates

Initial status update (short):

"We are investigating elevated error rates impacting model inference in us-west-2. Customers may experience increased latency or errors for text-generation and embeddings. Our engineering team is actively diagnosing. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or when we have material changes."

Customer incident bulletin (example for tenant impact):

Subject: Service impact — Redwood Inference (us-west-2) — 2025-02-14

Hello <CustomerName>,

We are actively investigating an incident affecting inference requests in the us-west-2 region which may cause increased latency and errors. Impact: ~12% of requests for text-generation routes may fail or time out. Our engineers have applied a traffic-level mitigation (routing to fallback-variant) and are monitoring.

What we are doing:
- Containment: routed traffic to fallback model-variant to restore availability
- Remediation: investigating root cause (scheduler backlog + KV cache pressure) and preparing safe rollout of a fix
- Next update: within 30 minutes or sooner if the situation changes

We apologize for the disruption. Your assigned CS lead, <CSL name>, is available at <csl@redwood.ai> for account-specific questions.

Post-incident summary (customer-facing) template (after RCA complete):

Subject: Incident summary — Redwood Inference (us-west-2) — 2025-02-14

Hello <CustomerName>,

Summary: On 2025-02-14 from 09:12–10:06 UTC, some inference requests in us-west-2 experienced elevated latency and error rates. Root cause: a combination of rapid configurational rollout to router replicas and an unexpected KV cache eviction spike that caused request queuing and backend timeouts.

Impact: Estimated 8–15% of requests for text-generation routes experienced errors or increased latency.

Actions taken:
- Immediate routing to fallback variant to restore availability
- Reverted the router configuration and restored a known-good KV cache snapshot
- Added additional capacity to dedicated-proxy pool and tightened autoscale thresholds

Preventative measures:
- Add pre-deploy canary that runs traffic at production concurrency for router rollouts
- Instrument KV cache eviction metric alerts and automated warm-up jobs
- Extend runbook steps for batch-size throttling and safer rollback tooling

We value your trust and are available to discuss further.

Runbook snippets and CLI examples

Check active queues on scheduler (kubectl-like):

kubectl -n inference get jobs | grep scheduler | xargs kubectl -n inference logs -f

Trigger traffic routing (ops-api):

curl -X POST "https://ops-api.redwood.internal/v1/route" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","target":"fallback-v1","reason":"auto-mitigation"}'

Post status page update (example JSON payload):

{
  "component": "inference (us-west-2)",
  "status": "degraded_performance",
  "message": "Investigating elevated errors and latency for inference requests. Mitigation in progress."
}

Sample Slack bridge messages (copy & paste)

Initial bridge message:
> [INCIDENT] inference-gateway/us-west-2 — Elevated 500s and p99 latency. FR: @priya (ack). Triage: checking scheduler/backends and recent deploys.

Status update at 30m:
> [UPDATE] Mitigation applied: routing to fallback variant. Observed p99 reduced from 1.2s -> 260ms. Continuing monitoring.

Postmortem scaffold (internal)

1. Summary (2–3 sentence executive synopsis)
2. Timeline (minute-resolution)
3. Impact (customers affected, KPIs)
4. Root cause analysis (tech detail + evidence)
5. Actions taken (containment and remediation)
6. Action items (owner, ETA, verification method)
7. Lessons learned & follow-ups (game-day adjustments)

Action item table (example)

| Action | Owner | ETA | Verification |
|--------|-------|-----|--------------|
| Add canary traffic harness for router rollouts | infra-team | 2025-04-01 | Canary run report + SLO pass |
| KV cache eviction alert added with 5m window | eng-sre | 2025-02-21 | Alert firing test + runbook link |

Game-day syllabus (90-minute lab)

- Objective: practice rapid containment for KV cache corruption and router rollout regressions.
- Participants: 1 FR, 1 PP, 1 OCL, 1 CSL, 2 observers
- Agenda (90m):
  1. 0–10m: intro and goals, roles assigned
  2. 10–30m: inject simulated p99 spike via synthetic load to inference-gateway
  3. 30–45m: FR performs triage and applies containment (route to fallback)
  4. 45–60m: Platform Pager investigates infra; OCL coordinates customer notice draft
  5. 60–75m: Remediation steps and rollback exercise
  6. 75–90m: Retro and capture improvements to runbook

Maintaining the chronicle (doc governance)

- Every major runbook change must include a one-line summary and link to the game-day where it was validated.
- Postmortem owners must create action items with clear owners and verification steps; unverified actions older than 45 days escalate to SRE Manager.
- Quarterly review: OCL and SRE Manager review the top 5 incident classes and ensure playbooks remain current.

Appendix: quick reference snippets and links

- Incident bridge channel: #inc-bridge
- Ops API: https://ops-api.redwood.internal/docs
- Runbook library index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-library
- Pagerduty schedule: Redwood-Platform-Oncall

This document is intended as a compact operational chronicle linking runbooks, comms, and learning. For detailed per-service runbooks, see the runbook-library and service-specific playbooks linked in Related Pages above.
